items.title: ExcalidrawZ: Local Native Excalidraw on macOS/iOS
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/chocoford/ExcalidrawZ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50468944 Points: 61 # Comments: 18
items.content:
Excalidraw is an excellent drawing tool. ExcalidrawZ keeps the familiar Excalidraw canvas, then adds native file management, iCloud sync, history, export, AI assistance, MCP integration, and Apple-platform interaction details around it.

ExcalidrawZ manages drawings as real app documents instead of loose browser downloads.

ExcalidrawZ records checkpoints for app-managed drawings, so you can review earlier versions and restore important work when needed.

The canvas remains compatible with Excalidraw while the surrounding app is built for Apple platforms.

Use Excalidraw collaboration when you want to draw with others.

ExcalidrawZ includes an AI assistant designed for canvas work.

ExcalidrawZ can expose the current app as an MCP server for compatible AI clients.

ExcalidrawZ includes richer tools for technical drawings and study notes.

For sensitive drawings, ExcalidrawZ adds protection around both storage and AI access.

ExcalidrawZ can open, import, edit, or export common Excalidraw-related formats:

Welcome to my Discord server to share suggestions or report issues for ExcalidrawZ.

Create Config/Overrides.xcconfig relative to the repository root, alongside Config/Project.xcconfig :

Replace these example values with identifiers registered to your Apple Developer team. The shared configuration leaves DEVELOPMENT_TEAM empty; set your team in the local overrides. The app and QuickLook extension must use the same App Group. All targets, including the extension and tests, inherit the team from Config/Project.xcconfig , which includes your local overrides. These overrides apply to all build configurations.

Create Config/Secrets.plist relative to the repository root. The project already references this file and includes it in both app targets' resources. The app's configuration loader stops with Unable to load Secrets.plist if the file is missing or invalid.

For local drawing development, this minimal configuration is sufficient:

COLLAB_URL must be a valid absolute URL. The example URL is a placeholder for local drawing work; to test collaboration, replace it with the URL of your deployed collaboration-enabled Excalidraw web client.

Optional string keys are ONEDRIVE_CLIENT_ID , GOOGLE_DRIVE_MACOS_CLIENT_ID , and GOOGLE_DRIVE_IOS_CLIENT_ID . Configure your own OAuth client IDs when developing the corresponding integrations.

Config/Overrides.xcconfig and Config/Secrets.plist are ignored by Git and should stay local.

items.title: I'm making LLMs work on small and old devices
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/hyperionaidev/smolmaxxing/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50468888 Points: 129 # Comments: 51
items.content:
Every device around you is more capable than it looks. TV boxes, old phones, single-board computers and routers all ship with CPUs, RAM and flash that sit idle most of the day. smolmaxxing is about unlocking that capability: finding the biggest language model each device can really run, then pushing it further with custom kernels, smarter memory use and weight streaming. Every claim is measured on the hardware itself.

Device #1 is a Xiaomi TV Box S (3rd Gen) : Amlogic S7D, 4× Cortex-A55 @ 2.5 GHz, 1.9 GB of RAM (about 1 GB usable), eMMC flash, Android 14, no root. On it, this repo runs models from 260 K to 16 B parameters:

Device #2 is a first-generation iPad Air (2013) : Apple A7, 2 cores, NEON without dotprod, 1 GB of RAM , iOS 12.5.7, jailbroken, CPU only. A 13-year-old tablet runs a 1.7B-parameter model at 24-26 tok/s (18-22 in long chats), a 4B one at about 10 tok/s , an 8B mixture of experts at about 3.5 tok/s (5 with half its experts, at a quality cost), and a 16B one at 2.6-4.5 tok/s , with their experts paged from flash, from a chat page in its own Safari. See Results on device #2 .

Every step is written up experiment by experiment in EXPERIMENT.md (E1-E160).

The techniques aren't tied to one box. The 1-bit lookup-table kernel needs only base NEON, as the iPad shows; any ARM chip with dotprod gets the other kernels; and any Linux or Android device with more model than RAM can use the streaming engine.

On this box, the 2B is the best speed-quality balance. Ling-mini-2.0 shows that bigger isn't automatically better: it is twice Moon-Beam's size, but scores worse per byte and runs slower.

What we built, grouped by the bottleneck it attacks (details and numbers in What's in here ):

Quality is English perplexity on a fixed 22 KB text, converted to bits per byte so models with different tokenizers compare fairly (lower is better). Speed is generation on the TV, measured either through llama-server with real chat requests ("chat") or with llama-bench ("bench").

* measured on the pruned head's positions (1.3 % of tokens fall outside it), so not exactly comparable; the stock full-vocabulary Q4_0 file scores 1.024.

Granite 4.0 H 1B was the one model close to the 2B's quality. Rebuilt our way (E62), it runs at 5.29 tok/s, below the 2B's 6.55 at slightly lower quality: it carries about twice the 0.8B's weight bytes per token.

Physics of the box: one process can hold ~0.96 GB before Android starts killing things (~1.15 GB in headless mode, with the launchers and Google services force-stopped), and flash reads top out at 278 MB/s , with a lone ~1 MB random read costing ~6 ms. A model that has to stream X MB per token can never beat 278 / X tokens per second. That, not the CPU, is what limits everything above 2B, and why a mixture-of-experts model, which touches ~1 B of its 8 B weights per token, is the way past it.

10 tok/s at 8 B? Measured, not guessed (E98): Moon-Beam reaches 10.4 tok/s with 2 experts per token, but the text turns to gibberish; the best coherent setting is ~7-8 tok/s. Dense Qwen3-8B is Bonsai-8B at 1 bit, and the smallest Qwen MoE (35B-A3B) touches 3× Moon-Beam's weights per token.

A 2013 iPad Air: Apple A7, 2 cores, NEON without dotprod, 1 GB of RAM, iOS 12.5.7, jailbroken with Amethyst . Everything runs on the CPU with 2 threads and a 1,024-token context, cross-compiled from a Mac. The write-up is §21 of EXPERIMENT.md , and build steps are in ipad-air/README.md .

Only the Bonsai and Moon-Beam rows were measured on the latest build. The other rows predate the attention and sampler work below.

"Can't load": iOS 12 lets a process map at most about 1.7 GB, so stock llama.cpp fails on the 2.6 and 5.5 GB files before running a token. "First run" for Moon-Beam is the first expert-pager run (pool 8, no bias).

What we built on the iPad, grouped by the bottleneck it attacks:

How Bonsai-1.7B got from 2.75 to about 25 tok/s (same model file throughout):

In long chats (400-token answers), the three turns went from 15.4 / 7.6 / 8.2 to 21.8 / 17.9 / 18.4 tok/s through the attention work alone. The pruning threshold that holds long chats above 17 costs +0.42 % perplexity at 1,024 tokens of context, near the ±0.3 % noise floor; GGML_FA_EPS=0.0001 trades that back for about 15 tok/s.

An 8B model, through an expert pager. iOS 12 caps a process at about 1.7 GB of mapped address space (1.3 GB for the web server's user), so Moon-Beam-8B's 2.6 GB file can't even be mapped, and keeping fewer experts to make it fit more than doubles its perplexity (§21.7). Dense Bonsai-8B runs at 0.08 tok/s from flash. So the model file is rewritten with its experts last, only the 474 MB before them is mapped, and each layer keeps 14 experts in RAM, reading the others from flash with pread when the router picks them. Results match the unpaged model exactly. A small routing bias toward experts already in RAM (+0.3 % perplexity, inside the noise) brought it to 2.4-2.8 tok/s in about 600 MB (§21.8). Round 2 (§21.9) queues flash reads by when they're needed, prefetches the next layer's likely experts, and runs the experts through a lookup-table kernel for Q2_K: 3.4 tok/s, 40× the dense 8B, at +0.7 % perplexity on the full eval text. The flash is still the limit: each token reads about 53 MB at 266 MB/s. Wiring weights in RAM kernel-panicked the iPad, like a pool of 16 did before. Round 3 (§21.10) evicts by decayed use frequency instead of recency, for 3.5 tok/s at no quality cost. 5 tok/s takes 4 experts per token instead of 8 (+27 % perplexity); choosing the count per token adaptively turned out no better than a fixed count. A 16B model (§21.11): Ling-mini-2.0, 16.3B parameters with 256 small experts per layer, runs through the same pager at 2.6 tok/s with unchanged routing, 3.3 at +2.6 % perplexity and 4.5 with a strong cache bias , in under 580 MB. Its 5.5 GB file was assembled from two published quantizations over HTTP range requests and streamed straight to the iPad, since the Mac had no room for it. It is twice Moon-Beam's size at the same speed, but not a better model (+3 % perplexity).

Limits worth knowing. Bonsai is a 1-bit model and still gets facts wrong (in one test it called Mercury the closest planet to Earth). About 700 MB is the practical memory ceiling: 1-bit weights don't compress, so iOS starts killing processes past it, which is why the 4B needs a 512-token context. The jailbreak doesn't survive a reboot. The fast output head adds 2-3 s to the first prompt after each launch.

Kernels for Cortex-A55 (ARMv8.2 dotprod, no i8mm) , as a patch on llama.cpp v0.8.0, each with an exactness test against a scalar reference:

Headless mode ( tools/tv-llm-mode.sh on|off ): a small foreground activity, then the launchers, Google services and other heavy apps are force-stopped, and svc power stayon keeps the animated screensaver (17 % of a core) away. Nothing persistent except stay-awake, which off restores. MemAvailable ~1000 → ~1300 MB. A fork-free guard ( tools/tv-watch.c ) replaced a shell loop that started ~25 processes a second and cost 10 % of the speed.

Expert pager for mixture-of-experts models ( ggml-cpu/moe-pager-tv.inc ):

Weight streaming for models bigger than RAM ( ggml-cpu/stream-tv.inc ):

Profiling (env switches in the patch): GGML_OPPROF=1 per-op table, GGML_OPPROF=2 a node-by-node, per-thread trace of one graph ( tools/optrace.py ), LLAMA_UBATCH_PROF / GGML_CPU_PROF phase timings. They showed where a small model's time really goes (E57): ~71 % Q4_K matmuls, and only ~2 ms per token of barriers and scheduling.

You need: the TV box (or another ARMv8.2 Android device) with network ADB, adb , zig (for static aarch64 musl builds), cmake + ninja , python3 , and uv (for numpy).

Everything on the box lives in /data/local/tmp/llm and runs as the adb shell user. The only system setting touched is stay-awake in headless mode ( svc power stayon ), which tv-llm-mode.sh off turns back off. adb shell rm -rf /data/local/tmp/llm removes it all.

The model files (0.5-4 GB each) are not in this repo. tools/rebuild-models.sh recreates every one from public Hugging Face files, streaming them through tools/gguf_build.py onto the TV. The SHA-256s below are of the files used in the experiments. Rebuilds of the 4B, Bonsai-8B and 9B files were checked byte-identical .

Ready-made downloads. The best file of each size class is on Hugging Face exactly as the TV runs it. They need the patched llama.cpp above; stock llama.cpp can't load the pruned head. Each card has the run command and the measured numbers:

Download with hf download hyperionaidev/ --local-dir models/ , then adb push the files to /data/local/tmp/llm/ , with moe-warm-*.txt next to them. That replaces the 08 / 2b / 4b / mb / b8 / lm targets. For the 8B and 16B models, the first start writes the repack cache.

iPad Air downloads. Every model run on the iPad, where to get it, and its speed there. The three MoE files are our own builds, laid out for the iPad's expert pager and lookup-table kernel: they need the iOS 12 patch ( ipad-air/ ), and any other llama.cpp loads them but gets scrambled experts. The rest are used exactly as published; the Bonsai models' fast layouts are built in RAM at load time. 53 experiments in all (E108-E160, §21):

items.title: Manovra, l’Upb boccia le misure sulla sanità. Giorgetti: “Su pensioni differenze incostituzionali”
items.summary: Proseguono le audizioni davanti alle commissioni Bilancio di Camera e Senato. Il testo, dopo il vertice di maggioranza di ieri, sarà sottoposto a modifiche
items.content:
ROMA – Ultima giornata di audizioni sulla manovra davanti alle commissioni Bilancio di Camera e Senato. Il testo, dopo il vertice di maggioranza di ieri, sarà sottoposto a modifiche. Palazzo Chigi aveva chiarito di essere al lavoro su “ un pacchetto concordato di emendamenti ”. Su quattro ambiti, in particolare: scuola, sanità, pensioni e università. Proprio sulla sanità attacca l’ Ufficio parlamentare di bilancio (Upb): “Si sottolinea la criticità della scelta di destinare al sostegno della domanda di prestazioni prevalentemente private quasi il 40% delle risorse destinate alla sanità, equivalenti al 70% dell'incremento del finanziamento ordinario del Ssn previsto per il 2027, anziché convogliarle al potenziamento dell'offerta pubblica”, rimarca la presidente dell'Upb Lilia Cavallari .

Giorgetti: accetto le critiche di misura sudamericana ma rivendico politica asburgica

Manovra: Giorgetti, prudenza conti per affrontare difficoltà

Upb: criteri Carta anziani non garantiscono risorse raggiungano più bisognosi

Upb: al privato quasi il 40% delle risorse per la sanità, a scapito del pubblico

Giorgetti: sull'età per le pensioni differenze inique e anticostituzionali

Sulle pensioni "si tratta individuare forme di flessibilità e adesso vedremo le proposte che vengono avanti. Però, quello che ho sempre detto e che ribadisco è che c'è un'incredibile sperequazione , che a mio giudizio è anche incostituzionale, tra chi ha cominciato a contribuire prima del 96 dopo il 96 introdotta la legge Fornero". Lo afferma il ministro dell'Economia, Giancarlo Giorgetti, durante l'audizione sulla manovra. "Se hai cominciato a contribuire dopo il 96 hai determinate agevolazioni di uscita (come la pensione anticipata a 64 anni, ndr ), se sei nato disgraziatamente nell'età felice del boom economico invece no. Sarebbe il caso, in qualche modo, di affrontare con un po’ di equilibrio ed equità il tema", aggiunge, "come sempre le analisi che faremo saranno basate sulla sostenibilità del sistema nel lungo termine ".

Giorgetti: gara per gestione fondo nuovi nati? Totalmente aperto

"Una gara rispetto all'assegnazione di Cdp" alla gestione del Fondo nuovi nati? "Sono totalmente aperto: se qualcuno è in grado fare condizioni migliori, perché no, alla gara non ho nessun tipo di contrarietà". Lo ha detto il ministro dell'Economia Giancarlo Giorgetti rispondendo alle domande dei parlamentari in audizione sulla manovra.

Giorgetti: risorse su payback per evitare che imprese e Regioni collassino

Sulla sanità "una delle voci che nessuno richiama si chiama payback . Non l'abbiamo fatto noi, ma giustamente interveniamo e mettiamo risorse per fare in modo che il sistema delle imprese e anche le Regioni non collassino ". Lo ha detto il ministro dell'Economia e delle Finanze, Giancarlo Giorgetti, in audizione davanti alle commissioni Bilancio di Camera e Senato sulla manovra.

Giorgetti: su cybersicurezza spero evoluzione nell'Ue per uso Nec difesa

Sull'emergenza cybersicurezza "spero che ci sia un'evoluzione, ad esempio la Nec difesa: spero che in Europa si capisca quanto sia importante questo aspetto, anche per la regola". Lo ha detto il ministro dell'Economia Giancarlo Giorgetti interpellato sull'emergenza cybersicurezza a margine dell'audizione alle commissioni Bilancio di Camera e Senato sulla manovra. "Sulla cyber spero che l'evoluzione che sta maturando a livello europeo rispetto ai rischi posti da questo tema è che possano essere associati all'utilizzo della Nec difesa. In questo momento ancora no, penso che sia questione di settimane e che si possa ricadere lì", ha detto Giorgetti rispondendo alle domande dei parlamentari.

"Le stime presentate oggi dall'Ufficio parlamentare di bilancio confermano tutte le nostre preoccupazioni: questa manovra è profondamente iniqua e accentua le disuguaglianze. Il taglio dell'Irpef premia soprattutto i redditi più alti : ne beneficia l'89% dei dirigenti, con 444 euro medi, contro appena l'1% degli operai, che riceveranno 4 euro. Il ministro Giorgetti è stato incapace di smentire l'allarme dell'Upb e le gravi disparità evidenziate dai suoi dati. Si è limitato a rivendicare la coerenza della manovra con il programma della destra. Ma è proprio questa la contestazione: una legge di Bilancio che non affronta le vere emergenze del Paese, dal caro vita alla crisi della sanità pubblica". Lo dice la capogruppo del Pd alla Camera, Chiara Braga , aggiungendo che " le Regioni chiedono almeno altri 4 miliardi per il Servizio sanitario nazionale. Le risorse aggiuntive stanziate dal governo sono insufficienti e in parte vincolate" e "mancano gli investimenti necessari per sostenere la crescita e affrontare la fine del Pnrr, che in questi anni ha rappresentato il principale motore degli investimenti pubblici, contribuendo a evitare la recessione". "Siamo inoltre preoccupati per l'approssimazione e la confusione con cui la maggioranza sta affrontando questo passaggio parlamentare, prefigurando riscrittura totali della manovra su temi centrali e trasformandola in uno strumento di propaganda elettorale anziché in un'occasione per rispondere ai bisogni degli italiani. Senza interventi adeguati, il Paese rischia di pagare un prezzo alto, sul piano sociale, sanitario ed economico", conclude Braga.

Giorgetti: opposizione vicina a banche, noi continuiamo una politica asburgica

" Voi dell'opposizione, che siete vicini alle banche , fatelo un intervento per le banche e noi saremo contenti di rinnovare la nostra politica asburgica e anche per l'ultimo scorcio di legislatura farci carico di questo onere". Lo afferma il ministro dell'Economia, Giancarlo Giorgetti, replicando ai parlamentari durante l'audizione sulla manovra.

"Quando presento la legge di bilancio devo essere sicuro di avere concordato le misure con la Commissione europea ". Lo ha sottolineato il ministro dell'Economia, Giancarlo Giorgetti, replicando durante l'audizione sulla manovra. Il ministro ha ricordato che il dettaglio degli interventi legati alla clausola di salvaguardia è stato trasmesso al Parlamento il 2 novembre e che l'Ecofin ha successivamente approvato la struttura delle proposte italiane. L'obiettivo, ha spiegato, è evitare di presentare misure che possano essere successivamente contestate da Bruxelles e debbano quindi essere corrette.

"Certamente non abbiamo potuto coprire tutto quello che avremmo voluto fare. Il momento è del tutto particolare". Lo ha ammesso il ministro dell'Economia, Giancarlo Giorgetti, concludendo la replica durante l'audizione sulla manovra davanti alle commissioni Bilancio di Camera e Senato. "Ci siamo sforzati di venire incontro ad alcuni temi che sono stati sollevati, primo fra tutti quest'anno il tema dei giovani", ha spiegato il ministro, sottolineando che le risorse disponibili sono state concentrate su incentivi, decontribuzioni e detassazioni per favorire l'occupazione. "Dobbiamo cercare di portare il più possibile i giovani che oggi sono disoccupati o Neet nel mondo del lavoro", ha aggiunto Giorgetti.

Giorgetti: accetto le critiche di misura sudamericana ma rivendico politica asburgica

" Accetto le critiche di una misura sudamericana ma rivendico la politica asburgica di questi 4 anni ". Lo ha detto il ministro dell'Economia Giancarlo Giorgetti rispondendo alle domande dei parlamentari in audizione sulla manovra in merito alle critiche dell'ad di Intesa Sanpaolo Carlo Messina per la norma sul superbonus in legge di bilancio. "È stata contestata la misura sul Superbonus in 10 anni, definita da Carlo Messina una misura sudamericana: però vorrei sottolineare che è lo spalmamento di 23-24 miliardi di Superbonus. Invece un ministro asburgico si è fatto carico di assorbire nel bilancio dello Stato un totale di 140 miliardi di Superbonus. Senza questo apporto il rapporto debito-Pil sarebbe già disceso a 132", ha detto Giorgetti. "Questa è un'altra tramezza, messa lì per ricordare questo principio", ha aggiunto il ministro.

Giorgetti: da piccolo ho fatto il 'magutt', so che i muri portanti non si toccano

"Da piccolo durante le vacanze mio papà mi mandava a fare il 'magutt' (il muratore, ndr ) e conosco la differenza fra i muri portanti e i tramezzi: i muri portanti non si toccano, i tramezzi sì perché non fanno venir giù l'impianto. Questo tipo di approccio significa che su alcune questioni - nel momento in cui ci sono proposte coperte - io credo che il ministro non debba fare le barricate". Lo ha detto il ministro dell'Economia Giancarlo Giorgetti in audizione sulla manovra.

"Scopro che il mio destino sarebbe quello di una grande banca, non ne avevo conoscenza. Però dopo le dichiarazioni di oggi sicuramente sono fuori". Lo ha detto il ministro dell'Economia, Giancarlo Giorgetti, nelle repliche in audizione sulla manovra di fronte alle Commissioni Bilancio congiunte.

"Mi ricordo la prima seduta in cui mi contestavate che c'erano delle misure una tantum , anche il primo anno. Poi quelle misure , prorogate di anno in anno, sono diventate strutturali ". Lo ha affermato il ministro dell'Economia, Giancarlo Giorgetti, replicando alle osservazioni dei parlamentari durante l'audizione sulla manovra. "Mi auguro che avvenga anche in questo caso, però dipende dall'evoluzione politica e del momento", ha aggiunto il ministro, rispondendo alle critiche sulla natura temporanea di alcuni interventi previsti dalla legge di bilancio.

items.title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says
items.summary: Medical staff are going unpaid, lack proper training and are struggling with shortages of essential supplies, MSF warns
items.content:
Hundreds of millions of dollars meant to help tackle Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo are not reaching the intended recipients, a medical charity has warned.

A report from Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) said that while the outbreak remained "out of control", front-line workers were going unpaid, lacked proper training and were struggling with shortages of essential supplies.

More than 5,400 people have died and 11,000 infected with Ebola in DR Congo since the outbreak was declared in May.

This makes it the second-most deadly outbreak of the disease ever recorded.

MSF has urged the Congolese government and UN agencies to "strengthen oversight and accountability" to ensure money already disbursed is effectively utilised.

This means "ensuring response personnel are properly trained, paid, equipped, and supported, and directing resources towards areas where needs are greatest", it said.

MSF's warning adds to concerns raised by Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) last month, when it said that $700m (£527m) out of $962m disbursed to organisations implementing Ebola response was unaccounted for.

At the time, Africa CDC chief Jean Kaseya said it was too early to describe it as embezzlement, characterising the issue as a major transparency and financial reporting failure.

The Congolese health minister echoed these concerns, saying that aid agencies were required to provide details of their work so the ministry could provide oversight but that only 22% had done so.

"Our requirement is clear: transparency must be total. The response relies on a single plan, a single budget, and a single coordination," Health Minister Samuel-Roger Kamba said on X. , external

What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult?

In its report , external , the charity said: "Despite the vast amounts of money provided for the response, many frontline responders are left trying to contain the outbreak with empty hands and empty pockets."

It also mentioned Ebola monitoring "surveillance teams that exist on paper but are nowhere to be seen on the ground".

"Our teams are often left speechless by the dysfunctions they witness in many areas. Six months into the response, this situation is simply unacceptable," said MSF president Javid Abdelmoneim.

One important way of stopping Ebola from spreading is contact tracing - finding all those people who had come into contact with an infected person and putting them into isolation.

"Despite the resources officially allocated to this critical activity, surveillance remains deeply problematic," MSF said, adding that two-thirds of deaths were occurring in communities not treatment centres.

According to British epidemiologist Neil Ferguson, more than half of the cases are going undetected, meaning the outbreak is likely to last another year, reports the Reuters news agency.

MSF also raised concerns over "excessive concentration" of efforts in certain areas at the expense of other areas where needs were more urgent.

It said the response was "too slow" in North Kivu province while Haut-Uélé remained "dramatically overlooked".

In both provinces, MSF observed that teams were "inadequately resourced to respond effectively" with health facilities lacking essential items such as water, chlorine or triage systems.

"This has turned some facilities into new centres of transmission, rather than places of care that contribute to containing the disease," MSF said.

The epicentre of the outbreak is in eastern DR Congo, which has been wracked by conflict for many decades, with some affected areas under rebel control.

There are very few good roads in the area, making it very hard to travel around.

On Thursday, the UN and government warned that the areas worst affected by Ebola were also suffering from a severe food crisis, with almost 10 million in the region in dire need.

The latest outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo species of the virus, has spread beyond DR Congo borders, with cases reported in Kenya, Uganda and Nigeria.

On Wednesday, the last person infected with Ebola in Kenya was discharged, marking a major milestone in efforts to contain the disease in the East African nation .

The Bundibugyo species is relatively rare and has no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way.

items.title: Oura investe 625 milioni nella salute digitale, acquisita Counsel Health
items.summary: Oura acquisisce Counsel Health per 625 milioni e punta su AI medica e consulti direttamente nell'app.
items.content:
Oura ha deciso di investire 625 milioni di dollari per acquistare Counsel Health, una società americana che combina intelligenza artificiale e assistenza medica a distanza. L'accordo, annunciato il 10 novembre, dovrebbe essere completato entro la fine del 2026 e di fatto ci dice dove vuole arrivare il produttore del celebre anello intelligente. Perché limitarsi a raccogliere informazioni sulla salute, quando si possono aiutare gli utenti a capire cosa farne?

In realtà le due aziende collaboravano già da alcuni mesi, ma ora attraverso l'app Oura, gli utenti statunitensi che attivano il servizio Counsel possono rivolgere domande a un assistente AI capace di utilizzare anche i dati biometrici registrati dall'anello. Se la situazione richiede una valutazione clinica, è possibile passare dalla conversazione automatizzata a quella con un medico abilitato, senza uscire dall'applicazione.

L'idea è mettere insieme informazioni che normalmente rimangono separate, con Oura Ring che segue nel tempo parametri come sonno, frequenza cardiaca e altri indicatori fisiologici. Mentre un medico, durante una visita tradizionale, deve spesso ricostruire quanto accaduto nelle settimane precedenti attraverso il racconto del paziente, Counsel può utilizzare quei dati come parte del contesto, insieme alla storia clinica e ai sintomi riferiti, lasciando comunque al professionista sanitario le decisioni mediche.

items.title: Fitting Four 32 GB Resizable Bars Behind a PCIe Switch on Linux
items.summary: Article URL: https://doug.sh/posts/gpu-bars-behind-a-pcie-switch/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50468720 Points: 43 # Comments: 19
items.content:
My PCIe switch is a Broadcom PEX88096 in the board's one x16 slot, with four AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700s and the two RTX 3090s from my PCIe splitter post behind it, and the build post has the whole box.

The switch gives each card eight lanes and lets the cards copy to each other without going through the CPU. AMD's ROCm calls that peer-to-peer (P2P), and it only turns it on when each card's whole 32 GB is mapped. On Linux, that means a 32 GB Resizable BAR on every card. A base address register, or BAR, maps a range of the CPU's address space onto a device's memory. Resizable BAR is the BIOS option that lets a card's BAR be the full 32 GB instead of the default 256 MB.

A few people asked for the module after the build post, so it's on GitHub as gpu-rebar-layout . It leans on kernel internals that could change in any release, so read the README before you load it. A patch series on the mailing list fixes the sizing bug, but this board will still need the module's resize and rescan after it lands, with its padding turned off ( pad=0 ).

With the 3090s added, the board stopped at the white VGA light on its POST LEDs, because every 32 GB BAR takes up 64 GB of the BIOS's address space. The address space post has the math.

This board's BIOS has no per-card Resizable BAR setting. Linux can give large BARs to some cards and leave others small, as long as it does it before any GPU driver loads. With all six cards in and Resizable BAR off, I wanted Linux to do the allocation. The plan was to set each R9700's BAR size register to 32 GB, remove the CPU port the switch hangs off, and rescan, so the kernel lays out the whole switch again from the new sizes.

Each R9700's 32 GB BAR is followed by a doorbell BAR, for registers the driver writes to tell the card there's new work. With Resizable BAR on, the BIOS makes it 256 MB. Linux leaves it at 2 MB.

The kernel gave the switch a window of about 128.6 GB. With the doorbell placed after each BAR, the way Linux 7.0 lays them out, the four windows span 224 GB (three 64 GB slots plus the last card's 32 GB and its doorbell). Two R9700s got their BARs, and the rest of the switch got nothing.

That was on 7.0.6. The unpatched v7.4-rc1 kernel placed three of the four in the control run that the Linux kernel patch-testing post (coming soon) covers.

0x800200000 is 32 GB plus 2 MB, one card's window. The kernel had sized the switch's window as the plain sum of its children: four of those plus the two 3090s' 288 MB windows.

The function is pbus_size_mem() in drivers/pci/setup-bus.c . For each child of a bridge it adds the child's size, or its alignment if that's bigger, to the total.

That leaves no gap when every child's size is a multiple of its alignment, which is true for ordinary BARs because they're powers of two. A GPU's window here is 32 GB plus 2 MB with a 32 GB alignment, so the sum leaves out the gap of almost 32 GB between one card's doorbell and the next card's start.

It's a known regression. Nikolas Britton reported it on linux-pci in September , and the thread's title describes my problem almost word for word.

Ilpo Järvinen, who maintains this code, has a fix in a 14-patch series of resource placement fixes , at v5 as of November 6 and not merged yet. I tested it and sent a Tested-by to the linux-pci mailing list. With it, all four R9700s get their 32 GB.

Even with the fix, this board still needs something to set the BAR sizes and rescan before the GPU drivers load, because amdgpu's resize at load time can't grow a window that other cards already sit in.

The kernel already knows how to raise a BAR's alignment without changing its size, but naming a device in the pci=resource_alignment= boot option uses the resizing mode instead. Asking for 32 GB alignment on an R9700 would also grow its small BARs, including the 512 KB register BAR, which can't be aligned to 32 GB below 4 GB.

The workaround is an out-of-tree module that runs from the initramfs, the tiny early-boot filesystem the kernel starts from, before any GPU driver loads. For each matching card it sets the BAR size register, then it removes the root port above the switch and rescans.

Between the scan and the address assignment it walks every bus segment under the switch. It raises each smaller 64-bit prefetchable BAR's alignment to the size of the largest 64-bit prefetchable BAR on that segment, and does the same for the other memory BARs as a separate group. Each R9700 window becomes exactly 64 GB and each 3090 window exactly 512 MB. Once every window is a multiple of its alignment, the kernel's allocator does the rest.

After a reboot the R9700s sat at 160, 224, 288, and 352 GB, the 3090s just above them, and amdgpu reported the whole card.

With the ACS redirect setting the box already had ( pci=disable_acs_redir= on the R9700 switch ports), P2P between the R9700s ran at 14.0 GB/s for every pair, which is what an eight-lane gen4 link delivers in practice, and all four copying in a ring at once moved 54.7 GB/s.

I had help with this one. Claude wrote the module with me, ran the commands and tests on the box over SSH, and helped me draft this post. I did the physical work, read all the words, checked the numbers, and rewrote anything that sounded like a chatbot, so the mistakes are mine.

items.title: Guida Michelin, 16 ristoranti neostellati: da Paestum ad Arzachena, da Napoli a Torino. Dove si trovano
items.summary: Il ricordo di Nadia Santini al cerimonia dell'annuncio
items.content:
Si aggiungono altri 16 indirizzi ai 341 ristoranti che detenevano la stella Michelin. L'annuncio al Teatro Municipale di Piacenza durante la presentazione della 72esima edizione della Guida Michelin Italia iniziata con un emozionante omaggio a Nadia Santini , chef del tristellato Il Pescatore, recentemente mancata, e il saluto video del ministro del Turismo Gianmarco Mazzi.

Le nuove étoile sono state assegnate ad Akoya, Christian Mandura e Alessandro Daddea (Torino) Amanõ, Vincenzo Sorvillo ( Cagliari), La Tea del Kosmo, Michele Talarico (Livigno, Sondrio), Osteria Arbustico, Cristian Torsiello (Paestum, Salerno), Tosca, Daniele Serra (Casole D'Elsa, Siena) 1224 Restaurant Cortina, Federico Rovacchi (Cortina D'Ampezzo, Belluno), Mamesa, Marc Bernhart (Burgusio, Bolzano) La Spigola, Roberto Pisano (Golfo Aranci, Olbia), Visione Restaurant, Samuele Murro (Barbaresco, Cuneo), Charleston by Giovanni Solofra, Giovanni Solofra, Manuel Motta e Roberta Merolli (Palermo), Casa Rapisarda, Alessandro Rapisarda (Numana, Ancona) Maxi, Emanuel Scotti (Vico Equense, Napoli), Ulìa, Salvatore Camedda (Azachena, Olbia), Casanova, Michele Panzarini (Polignano a Mare, Bari) Casa Romano, Luca Adobati (Alzano Lombardo, Bergamo) Quid, Juan Camilo Quintero (Roma).

Riconoscimento speciale Mindful Voices (nuova piattaforma editoriale globale lanciata dalla Guida Michelin che prende il posto della Stella Verde) a Jessica Rosval dello stellato Gatto Verde di Modena e a Fabrizio Caponi (L'Ciocio - Osteria di Suvereto - Livorno).

Premio Opening of The Year per un'apertura del 2026 particolarmente importante e significativa a Juan Camilo Quintero, chef del Quid a Roma. Premio Young Chef 2027 al più promettente giovane cuoco a Simone Lezzerini, 30 anni tra qualche giorno, di N'Uovo Vino e Cucina di Sutri (Viterbo) che ha ottenuto anche la sua prima Stella Michelin. Premio Passion Dessert per il miglior dessert a Lorelei di Sorrento (Ciro Sicignano). Sommelier award 2027 ad Andrea Bravaccini, Ristorante del lago & Bagno di Romagna. Marta Cottarella, fondatrice dell'Accademia Intrecci, ha premiato con Service Award 2027 il miglior operatore di sala del 2027, Stefania Lepore (Casa Klopè by Luigi Lepore a Francavilla Angitola).

items.title: Xbox, il gioco in cloud gratis ma con pubblicità è disponibile per tutti. Ma i titoli compatibili sono ancora pochi
items.summary: Dopo aver guardato alcuni annunci consecutivi, ci sono trenta minuti di gioco gratuito. Vale solo per i giochi che l'utente ha già acquistato ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
La selezione è ancora limitata e include giochi come Call of Duty Modern Warfare II e III, Genshin Impact, Killer Instinct, Marvel Rivals, Path of Exile e Where Wind Meet. In tutto circa novanta giochi sono compatibili con questa fruizione in cloud.

In sostanza, all'avvio del gioco e poi ogni trenta minuti appariranno vari annunci in successione da circa 20-30 secondi ciascuno , come capita con le piattaforme di streaming per film e serie TV.

Fra gli annunci può esserci anche l'autopromozione di Xbox, di Game Pass o dei servizi di Microsoft (a noi è capitato uno spot su Azure, per esempio).

Dal menu Xbox è possibile vedere in qualunque momento quanti minuti della sessione mancano prima che venga interrotta di nuovo dagli annunci. Passati i trenta minuti, scatta un'altra sessione di annunci per poter proseguire con ulteriori trenta minuti.

items.title: Atp Finals: Cobolli nel gruppo di Alcaraz, con Medvedev e Tiafoe
items.summary: Nell'altro girone con Zverev ci sono Shelton, Fils e Jodar
items.content:
Flavio Cobolli è stato sorteggiato nel gruppo Ivan Lendl delle Atp Finals di Torino . L'azzurro se la vedrà con Carlos Alcaraz , Daniil Medvedev e Frances Tiafoe. Nel gruppo dedicato a John McEnroe ci sono Alexander Zverev, Ben Shelton, Arhtur Fils e Rafael Jodar.

E' arrivato il momento di conoscere quali saranno le sfide dei grandi match della sesta edizione torinese delle Nitto Atp Finals, in programma dal 15 al 22 novembre all'Inalpi Arena di Torino.

Il grattacielo Intesa Sanpaolo ha ospitato oggi la cerimonia di sorteggio per la fase a gironi delle partite di singolo e di doppio del torneo .

Il formato delle Finals prevede infatti una fase a gironi con formula round robin, con gli otto giocatori e le otto coppie di doppio, suddivisi in due gironi da quattro.

I primi due classificati di ciascun gruppo accederanno alle semifinali.

Anche quest'anno Intesa Sanpaolo è host partner del torneo tennistico che incorona il maestro dei maestri.

Bolelli e Vavassori sorteggiati con le teste di serie n. 2 Simone Bolelli e Andrea Vavassori sono stati sorteggiati nel gruppo Mark Woodforde delle Atp Finals di Torino. I due azzurri, teste di serie numero 5, dovranno sfidare le teste di serie numero 2 Christian Harrison e Neal Skupski, i numeri 3 Marcel Granollers e Horacio Zeballos e i numeri 7 Kevin Krawietz e Tim Puetz.

items.title: Nvidia è tornata a perdere parecchio in borsa
items.summary: Il prezzo delle azioni è arrivato a perdere più del 10 per cento, a causa delle dimissioni del suo capo e delle conseguenze su tutto il settore tecnologico
items.content:
Giovedì il prezzo delle azioni della società statunitense di chip Nvidia è arrivato a perdere più del 10 per cento alla borsa a New York, dov’è quotata l’azienda. Il calo è dovuto alle dimissioni del suo amministratore delegato Jensen Huang, che ha fondato Nvidia ed è uno dei più influenti manager del settore tecnologico mondiale.

Nei giorni passati Huang si era ritrovato al centro di due scandali: domenica era stata resa nota una sua relazione extraconiugale con Alice Huang, un’imprenditrice cinese che secondo l’intelligence statunitense è una spia della Cina (i due non sono parenti). Mercoledì è emersa una sua seconda relazione extraconiugale, questa volta con Kimberly Powell, una sua diretta sottoposta nell’azienda. Il valore delle azioni di Nvidia era già calato nei giorni scorsi per via della notizia legata al possibile spionaggio della Cina.

Huang guidava Nvidia sin dalla sua fondazione, nel 1993, e sotto la sua guida la società è diventata la più importante del settore. È la seconda azienda al mondo per capitalizzazione dopo Apple ed è stata la prima società al mondo a valere più di 5mila miliardi di dollari (al momento vale poco meno di 4mila). Non solo: progetta i chip impiegati da quasi tutte le aziende del settore dell’intelligenza artificiale, e tra i suoi clienti ci sono aziende importanti come OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, Meta e Google.

Gli investitori temono che i guai di Nvidia possano pesare su tutto il settore tecnologico e sullo sviluppo dell’intelligenza artificiale, settore che negli ultimi anni è cresciuto enormemente e ha portato a grandi rialzi nei principali indici di borsa. Da tempo si discute se gli investimenti siano stati eccessivi, se si sia creata una bolla speculativa e nel caso cosa potrebbe farla scoppiare.

Jensen Huang durante un discorso a Berlino, Germania (AP/Markus Schreiber)

I chip di Nvidia hanno anche una rilevanza strategica a livello politico, perché sono così potenti e performanti che il governo statunitense ha vietato all’azienda di esportarne alcuni modelli in Cina, per evitare che il paese ottenga il primato tecnologico dell’intelligenza artificiale. Ciò ha reso Huang uno dei manager più ascoltati dal presidente Donald Trump, che negli ultimi due anni ha avuto un atteggiamento molto favorevole nei confronti dell’intelligenza artificiale e dei data center, le strutture composte da server e computer che servono per far funzionare moltissimi servizi online.

Il favore di Trump potrebbe però essere meno incisivo dal prossimo anno, cioè da quando il Partito Democratico statunitense prenderà il controllo del parlamento, dopo la storica vittoria alle elezioni di metà mandato di inizio novembre. Gli investitori temono infatti che i Democratici vogliano imporre una maggiore regolamentazione sul settore, e per questa ragione il valore dei titoli di alcune aziende tecnologiche era già diminuito nei giorni successivi alla loro vittoria elettorale.

items.title: Jensen Huang travolto dagli scandali: lascia Nvidia con effetto immediato
items.summary: Jensen Huang lascia Nvidia dopo 33 anni alla guida. Sullo sfondo due relazioni extraconiugali e le indagini su una dirigente legata alla Cina. Colette Kress assume il comando ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Jensen Huang si è dimesso da presidente e amministratore delegato di Nvidia e ha lasciato il consiglio di amministrazione con effetto immediato. Lo ha annunciato pochi minuti fa la società, che ha affidato la guida ad interim a Colette Kress, direttrice finanziaria dal 2013 , che conserverà anche quell’incarico.

Le dimissioni sono la conseguenza degli scandali legati a due relazioni extraconiugali. La prima, rivelata il 29 ottobre dal New York Times, è con Alice Huang – dirigente del cliente asiatico di Nvidia Megaspeed – che l’intelligence statunitense ritiene legata ai servizi cinesi. La seconda, rivelata dallo stesso quotidiano l’11 novembre, è con Kimberly Powell, responsabile della divisione sanità di Nvidia.

In un messaggio ai dipendenti pubblicato domenica, Jensen Huang ha ammesso la propria infedeltà nei confronti della moglie Lori Mills, con cui è sposato da 41 anni. Non ha però fatto il nome né di Alice Huang né di Kimberly Powell. Intervistato da Bloomberg il 29 ottobre, poche ore dopo le prime rivelazioni del New York Times, Jensen Huang aveva definito i propri rapporti con Alice Huang del tutto normali e legati esclusivamente agli affari con Megaspeed.

Il consiglio ha avviato la ricerca di un amministratore delegato definitivo e valuterà candidati interni ed esterni. Per la prima volta ha anche nominato un presidente del cda, Harvey C. Jones, ex amministratore delegato di Synopsys, secondo cui l’attività e i piani sui prodotti proseguiranno senza interruzioni.

Huang, cofondatore della società 33 anni fa, ne è anche il maggiore azionista con circa il 3,6% delle quote. Ha più volte detto di non credere nei piani di successione, e la stessa Nvidia, nel rapporto annuale depositato alla SEC a febbraio, circa i rischi aveva avvisato gli azionisti di dipendere molto dal suo gruppo dirigente storico e che una pianificazione inadeguata della successione, del trasferimento delle conoscenze e degli avvicendamenti avrebbe potuto compromettere la strategia e il successo dell'azienda nel lungo periodo.

I risultati del terzo trimestre fiscale di Nvidia saranno comunque presentati il 17 novembre, come già previsto dall’agenda della società.

items.title: Show HN: AI Red Lines – write down what would make you act on AI
items.summary: Article URL: https://yourairedlines.com Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50467880 Points: 24 # Comments: 15
items.content:
Decide now what would make you act on AI, and what you'd do. Then share it.

Sharing gives you a link and an image to post. Your red lines go on this page's public wall once you copy your link or post them. No account needed. Until you share, they stay in this browser. Who sees what

To change what you shared, edit your red lines above and press Update.

Writing a red line down is a start. These steps make it more likely you'll keep it. Do each one, or skip it, and the next one opens.

In 138 trials, keeping track of a goal helped nearly three times as much when other people could see it. Where this comes from

Send it to two people, and ask them where their red lines are. Copying your link, opening a post or taking the image also puts your red lines on this page's wall.

Each button opens a draft with your link, and nothing is posted until you press Post. Download the image to add it.

In those trials, people who were prompted to check on a goal did better at reaching it. Where this comes from

In those trials, keeping track helped more than twice as much when people reported to someone else. Where this comes from

A witness: someone who'll ask you about it if one of your lines is crossed.

Opens a draft, sent only when you press Send. It includes every finished line, even private ones.

In those trials, keeping track helped about one and a half times as much when people kept a written record. Where this comes from

The same review notes that people rarely check on a goal unless something prompts them. A date in your calendar is that prompt. Where this comes from

The reminder doesn't include your red lines, so keep your saved copy.

From a 2016 review of 138 trials with 19,951 people (Harkin and others, Psychological Bulletin ). In each trial, some people were prompted to keep track of a goal and others weren't. On average, the people who were prompted did better at reaching it.

Nearly all the trials were about health goals, like weight or blood pressure. Nobody has tested red lines for AI, so read this as a guide, not a promise. Writing a line down doesn't mean you'll keep it. These steps make it more likely.

Things that have happened in AI, with their sources. If one crosses one of your red lines, say so here and see what you said you'd do. Your answers stay in your draft.

Suggested by the news finder. Nothing appears on the page until you add it.

Joseph Rotblat was a Polish physicist working in Liverpool when the war began. In 1944 he went to Los Alamos with the British team on the Manhattan Project. He had one reason for being there: the fear that Nazi Germany would build an atomic bomb first.

By the end of 1944 it was clear Germany would not. The reason he had come no longer held, so he resigned and went back to Liverpool. He is the only scientist known to have left the project on grounds of conscience.

Most of us never write down why we're somewhere. When things change slowly, nothing tells us to stop. Rotblat had that moment because he knew his reason. This page started as The Rotblat Line, to help you write down yours: the specific things that would make you act, and what you'd do, whether that's quitting, speaking up or finally getting involved. He was born on 4 November, so that's the day it suggests re-reading your red lines each year.

items.title: Running web sites makes me not want to
items.summary: Article URL: https://lowkey.party/running-web-sites-makes-me-not-want-to Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50467869 Points: 68 # Comments: 41
items.content:
Several years ago now I started self-hosting things. Initially the learning process and how to set up everything drove me to eagerly keep learning more and more, and even how to manage keeping everything up and reliable. But then the LLM Scrapers arrived.

I looked at Anubis and decided I didn't want the delay loading for regular viewers, so moved to iocaine which is slightly different in what it does, and that was fine until so many scrapers hit my site that it saturated my upload with generated content feeding the them. So I removed it, watched iftop - for not even very long - over a few evenings and noted a bunch of IP ranges owned by cloud companies and the likes of Meta(Facebook) who's servers have zero reason to hit my sites. Pretty sure no one is sharing links to my blog there. Also Azure, Alibaba... and a bunch of others.

I do realise that scrapers are also using residential IP ranges via SDK pitched to app developers that add backdoors to utilise the connection for "other things" (I cbf finding a link to put here but you can search for them if you want to get even more depressed about the state of the web), but most of the traffic was from a small number of large cloud allocated /16 IP ranges so I just dropped those in nftables. I also added nft-blackhole with what seems to be a few not overly zealous IP lists, and it seems to help a bit too.

People who check my photography site would have noticed I haven't updated it in a couple of years now. I have talked about it a few years ago , but it is driving me to consider removing my photography website as it currently is, and just have links to sell physical zines per event.

This is more work for me, but it really irks me how entitled the corporate scraping of the web has become just so they can sell back to us a poor imitation of creativity. I do not want my time spent on something that ends up feeding that machine. Yes I know they are now buying books and destroying them to feed it new data because the online pool it slurps up is now so muddied with LLM slop that it corrupts its own training data, but it seems unlikely they would buy some shitty zine from a local photographer in New Zealand - and I can monitor that.

I watched a video recently where a bunch of devs said they miss the old web, when everyone had their own site. I can't see this being likely again with the amount of "legal" DDOS we have to put up with if we have a website hosted on our home server. You just can't be a casual tech enthusiast and have enough limiting/protection in place these days. A certain amount of knowledge and skill is required, unless you... pay another large corporate to be the CDN in front of it. And the amount of traffic I should be getting means I very much dislike that answer.

Maybe I will enjoy the zine/book-making process if I can streamline the process to a certain point. If I get something useful sorted, I will update here of course.

This is yet another post on the depressing reality of the current times and corporate tech over-reach. But maybe it will force me to make something that only exists in the physical world instead, so there is that for our silver lining.

items.title: La ricerca: l’IA non toglie la creatività alla Gen Z, ma fa risparmiare tempo
items.summary: Presentati oggi a Milano i risultati del Lenovo Generation Creation Report, che affronta il rapporto tra le nuove generazioni e l’utilizzo dell’IA. ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Il timore più diffuso è che l’intelligenza artificiale finisca per sostituire chi crea, e questo vale soprattutto per i giovani, molti dei quali vedono il loro futuro minacciato dall’arrivo dell’IA, che si prenderà inevitabilmente parte dei lavori per i quali molti ragazzi hanno iniziato un percorso di studi senza immaginare quello che sarebbe successo.

Eppure, se guardiamo ai risultati del Lenovo Generation Creation Report, realizzato da Ipsos Doxa e presentato oggi a Milano, i giovani italiani la vedono diversamente.

L’indagine ha coinvolto 1.000 persone tra i 18 e i 30 anni con interviste online, e l’esito è chiaro: l’83% degli intervistati è favorevole all’IA, ma ritiene importante che il risultato finale rifletta le proprie idee (il 41% lo ritiene molto importante, il 42% abbastanza).

Quando si chiede ai ragazzi della Gen Z per cosa usino l’IA, il 42% risponde che la usa soprattutto per ricevere suggerimenti e per sviluppare o strutturare le idee, pur precisando che il lavoro vero, il pensiero alla base, resta suo . Solo l’8% dichiara di affidarsi spesso al risultato dell’IA con poche modifiche, prendendo per buono quello che il modello suggerisce.

Su una cosa, però, molti concordano: il vantaggio principale non è tanto il risultato quanto il tempo risparmiato rispetto a quello che servirebbe per fare la stessa cosa senza IA. Secondo gli intervistati, senza l’IA il 48% ci metterebbe molto più tempo, il 18% sarebbe meno produttivo e il 16% avrebbe meno idee. Solo il 14% pensa che peggiorerebbe la qualità del risultato.

Dalla ricerca emerge anche un altro aspetto: vuoi per l’influenza dei social, che hanno permesso a tutti di esprimersi e di avere una vetrina, vuoi per l’aiuto dato proprio dall’IA, la Gen Z è una generazione che, rispetto a quelle precedenti, produce contenuti e non si limita a consumarli. L’88% degli intervistati ha svolto almeno un’attività creativa negli ultimi tre mesi, e la più diffusa è ovviamente la content creation (83%), con i contenuti per i social al 49%, i video al 46% e la grafica e le immagini al 42%. La programmazione è solo al 21% , segno che le nuove generazioni hanno già capito che la scrittura di codice è un’attività che con il tempo diventerà molto di nicchia.

Da dove nasce l’idea, quando si tratta di creare qualcosa? Secondo le risposte, la scintilla nasce per il 30% da un interesse personale, per il 20% da esigenze di studio o lavoro e per il 13% da momenti di riflessione. Per svilupparla, però, quasi uno su due (47%) guarda ai social. L’IA è già usata da circa un terzo e si colloca allo stesso livello dei motori di ricerca.

La prima reazione a un’idea, poi, è raramente impulsiva: il 51% cerca prima informazioni, il 41% prende appunti, il 37% organizza i pensieri e il 32% apre un chatbot di IA per avere altri spunti. Solo il 7% si mette subito al lavoro. Interessante il mix di chi prende appunti: anche se il 38% usa lo smartphone, il 20% preferisce ancora carta e quaderno.

Dalla ricerca emerge però anche la difficoltà più grande una volta avuta l’idea: trasformarla in qualcosa di concreto, che possa diventare anche la base per una professione o per una nuova azienda. Questo vale per il 18% degli intervistati, seguito dal 17% del campione, che invece trova più difficile capire da dove partire. Solo il 13% dice di fare fatica a trovare l’idea iniziale.

Quali dispositivi usa la Gen Z quando si tratta di creare contenuti? Il 63% dice di usarne più di uno per lo stesso lavoro, con lo smartphone che fa da filo conduttore: è il dispositivo presente in tutte le fasi, quello che guida la nascita dell’idea (46%) e la successiva condivisione (44%).

Nella fase di realizzazione crescono notebook e desktop: il notebook pesa di più nella revisione (27%), mentre il desktop è il dispositivo della produzione (26%, soprattutto tra i profili tecnici). Il tablet, invece, è indicato come dispositivo principale nella fase di realizzazione dal 15% degli intervistati ed è più usato dagli studenti e dai 18-24enni, che lo scelgono per lavorare in mobilità.

items.title: In che senso Beppe Sala non aveva la «conferma» di essere indagato
items.summary: Il sindaco di Milano ha parlato del «paradosso» di averlo saputo dai giornali, che violano spesso il segreto istruttorio
items.content:
Il sindaco di Milano Beppe Sala ha detto di non aver mai avuto la conferma di essere stato indagato nell’inchiesta sull’urbanistica, fino a quando non ha saputo della richiesta di archiviazione delle indagini arrivata martedì. «Il paradosso» ha detto durante un evento organizzato dal quotidiano Repubblica , «è che il giorno in cui ho saputo della richiesta di archiviazione ho saputo di essere stato iscritto nel registro degli indagati. Io non avevo mai avuto conferma di essere indagato».

È normale che un indagato non sappia che la procura sta facendo indagini su di lui, anzi è una procedura prevista dalla legge. Si chiama segreto istruttorio e serve a evitare che la notizia delle indagini in corso possa ostacolare la ricerca e l’acquisizione delle prove. Ci sono però delle deroghe: le persone per esempio vengono avvisate di essere indagate quando chi indaga ha bisogno di fare approfondimenti che richiedono la loro presenza, come un interrogatorio o accertamenti irripetibili. In quei casi gli indagati ricevono una informazione – chiamata anche avviso – di garanzia.

La procura non è tenuta ad avvisare una persona indagata nemmeno se alla fine delle indagini decide di chiedere l’archiviazione, come successo a Sala. Chiunque, in pratica, potrebbe essere indagato senza venirne mai a conoscenza, se la sua posizione viene poi archiviata (d’altra parte la sola indagine non implica alcuna colpevolezza). Se invece la procura ha intenzione di chiedere il rinvio a giudizio, l’indagato riceve un avviso di conclusione delle indagini preliminari, che lo mette al corrente delle indagini fatte e delle accuse.

Quando Sala dice che ha saputo ufficialmente di essere stato indagato solo con l’archiviazione, si riferisce probabilmente al comunicato stampa che la procura ha diffuso dopo aver depositato la richiesta di archiviazione, che lo menzionava esplicitamente. Nella parte finale del documento si parla infatti dell’assenza di prove per dimostrare le «contestazioni di induzione a dare o promettere indebita utilità svolte nei confronti del sindaco di Milano Giuseppe Sala».

items.title: Abandoned Quake 4 expansion finished by modders and now playable
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.moddb.com/mods/openq4/downloads/openq4-0141-windows-x64 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50467618 Points: 161 # Comments: 55
items.content:
openQ4 is a free, open-source engine and game-code replacement for Quake 4. Play the original campaign and multiplayer on today's Windows, Linux and Steam Deck, with widescreen support, smooth high-refresh motion and optional visual upgrades.

openQ4 0.14.1, the Awakening Edition: play the recovered Quake 4 expansion beside the original campaign, with stable shadow mapping, a new interface, Vulkan on Windows, smarter bots and an experimental Android app.

The Quake 4 expansion that never shipped is now playable. openQ4 0.14.1, the Awakening Edition , is out now, and it is the biggest update since 0.13.2. It brings a second campaign, stable shadow mapping, a rebuilt interface, Vulkan on Windows, smarter bots and an experimental Android app, then spends the extra weeks polishing all of it toward production quality.

0.14.0 was withdrawn soon after release, so for most of you this is the first look at everything below. 0.14.1 replaces it, with every 0.14 feature refined, fixed and optimized. It is a big step on the road to 1.0.

Raven Software and Ritual Entertainment built an expansion for Quake 4 that was never released. Justin Marshall recovered and published it, and openQ4 now plays it beside the original campaign: pick Single Player > Campaign and choose Quake 4 or The Awakening.

openQ4 ships none of the expansion's content; you supply the files. The Awakening guide shows how.

Prefer the original look? The classic screens and HUD are one setting away: seta ui_retained 0 .

Three code audits and static analysis fixed crash, memory-safety and save-restore defects throughout the engine and game code. Saves are now written in a portable format and reported only once they are safely on disk, and openQ4's own data ships as separate packs so future patches can be small downloads.

Experimental means experimental: VR has not yet been qualified on headset hardware, Android has been qualified on one phone so far, and The Awakening is built from unfinished alpha content, with full playthrough qualification still in progress. Your reports help.

Grab it from the openQ4 downloads here on ModDB, or get any package from the GitHub release page :

The full release notes list everything new since 0.13.2, with upgrade notes and known limitations.

0.14.1 is a deliberate push toward 1.0: fewer new experiments and more polish on what already exists. The same engine work now underpins the rebased openPREY and openD3 projects, which share fixes with openQ4 in both directions.

Thank you to Emile Belanger for the Android port, Justin Marshall for recovering and publishing The Awakening, Schnapple of Mac Source Ports for the signed macOS builds, akacross for tireless playtesting and pull requests, and everyone who reported issues after 0.14.0. Come and tell us how it plays in #openq4 on the DarkMatter Discord .

items.title: Before Scott Colom, these two men were the last black US senators from Mississippi
items.summary: The Democratic candidate won in a southern state that had not seated a black senator since 1874.
items.content:
After winning a close race in Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colom will become the state's first black US senator for more than 150 years, and the third in history.

It is a historic result in the deeply conservative southern state that last sent a Democrat to the US Senate in 1982, and had not seated a black senator since 1875.

Colom follows Hiram Revels, who became the first black person ever to serve in the chamber when he was seated from 1870 to 1871, and Blanche Bruce, whose term ran from 1875 to 1881. Revels and Bruce were both members of the Republican Party.

Revels was chosen as Mississippi's first senator after the Civil War, serving for just over a year and campaigning strongly for racial equality.

A few years later, Bruce, who was born into slavery, became the first black person to serve a full term in the US Senate. He remained in Washington after leaving the chamber and held a role in the Treasury.

Both terms came before the repressive Jim Crow laws began to enforce racial segregation across Mississippi and other southern US states.

A significant factor in Colom's victory was his success in mobilising young people and the state's large black population, who are expected to have turned out in high numbers.

In a victory speech, Colom referenced how Revels, who was a minister and served as a chaplain during the Civil War, gained support for his Senate campaign through his words.

"That's an example of the power of prayer, and through our history, there are so many people that lifted this state up through the power of prayer in very dark times," Colom said.

Prior to the result being called, the BBC spoke to students at Jackson State University, a historically black college in Mississippi. Many of them had voted for the first time and backed Colom.

"I really feel like a change is what we need," 18-year-old Jamyria Dunn said.

"I've had some amazing days in my life," she continued, "but seeing Mississippi, this state in particular, turn blue, would really bring a light to my heart that people just would not understand."

Democrat Scott Colom makes history as Mississippi's first black senator since 19th Century

items.title: Talking Zen 6 with Mike Clark at AMD In-Depth
items.summary: Article URL: https://chipsandcheese.com/p/talking-zen-6-with-mike-clark-at Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50467460 Points: 122 # Comments: 1
items.content:
Hello you fine Internet folks, I sat down with AMD’s Mike Clark to talk about Zen 6, the evolution from Zen 5 and what some of the differences are between Zen 6 and Zen 6c and what drove some of those changes.

The transcript below has been edited for readability and conciseness.

George Cozma: Hello, you fine Internet folks. We’re here at AMD In-Depth, where we’re talking about Venice. With me, I have a returning guest, Mike Clark. Would you like to tell the audience who you are?

Mike Clark: Hi, I’m Mike Clark, the original architect of Zen. Some people refer to me as “Zen Daddy.” I’ve been working on cores here at AMD for 33 years, and we’ve got another great one coming, so I’m very proud of the design team I get to represent here today.

George Cozma: I’ve had some hands-on time with Zen 6c. Let’s talk about the change that’s happened with Zen 6 and Zen 6c, what I refer to in my piece as the Zen 6 family. Why is it different from previous generations?

Mike Clark: Right. Starting with Zen 4, we’ve been going through this evolution of having two core families. Before, we were really just using the denser technology as an area play. In this generation, having learned a lot, as we were filling out that denser version of the core, we wanted to leverage it to add some extra IPC within the core. So if you look more in-depth at what we have, what used to be our classic design, we now think of as our high-frequency design. And our dense technology is now our top-of-the-line, no-questions-asked performance core, because we’ve also enabled the full L3 in that implementation, at 4MB per core. So we have 32 of those cores, 128MB of L3, and the highest IPC you can get in that core.

George Cozma: Awesome. So far, one thing I’ve noticed is that the vector scheduler is a bit bigger on Zen 6c. What was the reasoning for increasing that on Zen 6c?

Mike Clark: Well, that wasn’t the only thing we increased. One principle we follow is that we don’t want to create a delta between the two architectures that software has to be optimized for. We want them to have the same fit and feel, so the same optimizations apply to both. But because of its reduced frequency target, Zen 6c can have a little more capacity in the queues, since it doesn’t have to reach the maximum frequency the high-frequency core has to hit. The floating-point scheduler is just one example. There are other queues throughout the core that are larger in Zen 6c, to pull out a little more IPC and get a little more leverage in that SMT environment as well.

George Cozma: Interesting. Both Zen 6 and Zen 6c build on the design you had in Zen 5, and one of the interesting things with Zen 5 was the dual decode setup. Has the front end changed much to let a single thread make better use of both decode clusters?

Mike Clark: Yes. As you said, Zen 5 was a new foundation, with the ability to fetch two basic blocks and get them down the line. But it gets quite complicated with one thread running larger-footprint workloads, where some of it might be hitting the I-cache and some of it might be hitting the op cache, and you’re trying to get everything synced up. So we spent a lot of time optimizing that and making it more efficient from both a delivery and a power perspective: less power wasted, and more efficient delivery from that new front end.

George Cozma: Awesome. Going down into the execution engine, I also noticed that the number of integer multiply units has gone down from three to two. Could you talk a bit about what drove that choice?

Mike Clark: It really came out of the Zen 5 design, where we had a more unified scheduler. To make a scheduler simpler, you want the units it schedules into to be very uniform, and the way we had set up those schedulers, adding a third multiplier to the group it was scheduling into was easy and didn’t add complication. In Zen 6, we realized that to really scale out the architecture, we needed to go back to more distributed schedulers, which now schedule into the ALUs. We hadn’t seen much uptick from that extra multiplier on Zen 5, so to optimize the area and the schedulers, we went back to two multipliers.

George Cozma: Speaking of integer multiply, on the vector side you’ve added two more VNNI units. What was the impetus for adding them, and at what point in the design did you add them?

Mike Clark: As I said in the talk, these are long design programs. We weren’t designing Zen 6 to be an agentic core. When we started, no one was really even using that term. But Zen 5 was a whole new foundation for AI workloads, and we’ve always believed the core has a place in AI: orchestration, data type manipulation, smaller models. So we were always focused on making the core good at AI. It’s not going to beat a GPU, and that’s not the point. We realized we probably should have some more VNNI, given where we were seeing inference go, and the team rallied around that. It was kind of late, since these are long-lead projects and the floor plan was set, but the team rallied, we were able to squeeze a couple more VNNI pipes in there, and it was a big success.

George Cozma: Again on the vector side, one of the oddities of Zen 5 was that although the wires were all there, the load unit could only do two vector loads at a time. What changed within the Zen 6 core to allow four vector loads, assuming they’re either 128 or 256 bits?

Mike Clark: We can do the 256-bit loads. Since we were able to do two 512-bit loads, we already had 1,024 wires headed over there. Obviously, using them piecemeal versus as one contiguous set complicates the design. I think it’s something we always wanted to do on Zen 5, but with all the change and getting it working, we left that for the Zen 6 team, and they were awesome. We’re all really one team at AMD anyway, and sometimes things intersect at different points in the roadmap. This was the time to do it.

George Cozma: Speaking of bandwidth into the caches, the L2 in Zen 5 had some oddities where it couldn’t always hit 64 bytes per cycle on reads. What changed in Zen 6 to allow that? Because I’ve been able to measure it, and it does hit that.

Mike Clark: Honestly, sometimes you just don’t see some of these things. A lot of it was that we would be over-prefetching, and prefetches that hit in the L2 would be robbing L2 bandwidth. So we made sure we could sustain those prefetches alongside demand requests, reduce the conflicts, and deliver the full 64 bytes per cycle that we want.

George Cozma: Awesome. Circling all the way back to the front: the all-important branch predictor. There seems to have been a reduction in branch misprediction latency, so when you miss a branch, the number of cycles it takes to recover has gone down. What I also noticed, which is really neat, is that there wasn’t any reduction in accuracy. So how did you pull off not only a faster branch predictor, but one that’s even slightly more accurate than Zen 5’s already very accurate predictor?

Mike Clark: The branch prediction team, as you know, is very algorithmic. There’s lots of design space and lots of exploration, and AI has even been getting involved in helping us figure out how to optimize it. It’s a great optimization problem: the number of TAGE tables, how much information they hold, accuracy. So we set out to make a more efficient one. That was an area where we didn’t really want to grow; we thought we could be more efficient in the way we lay out the tables for prediction. And we’re always focused on our pipeline length. No matter how good a branch predictor you build, there are always hard-to-predict branches, and you’re always going to mispredict. So each generation, we’re monomaniacally focused on getting going again as fast as we can when we’re wrong. There are lots of unique tricks we pull to get that redirect back into the front end and get it flowing as fast as possible. And you’ve observed it, which is great.

George Cozma: Yeah. I haven’t had time on Zen 6 yet, but I have had time on Zen 6c, and in SPECint 2026 it matches your fastest Zen 5 server CPU. That’s very impressive, especially considering the clock deficit. Wrapping this all up and moving outside the core into the L3, there are obviously topology differences between the 12-core and 32-core CCDs. How much were you able to mitigate those differences inside the core, building up structures to tolerate latency, to compensate for the slightly increased L3 latency?

Mike Clark: As I always talk about, the design has to be balanced. As we grow the capacity of a structure, the new technology helps it shrink, so the physical distance doesn’t grow linearly, but unfortunately the distance does grow. Inside the L3, there are a lot of tricks I can’t talk about...

Mike Clark: [In order to] maintain bandwidth within the L3 mesh so we can keep delivering to the cores. And in the cores, we do grow the queues to handle those higher latencies.

George Cozma: Awesome. My penultimate question: Verano is adding LPDDR5X to the EPYC ecosystem. Were there any design considerations between LPDDR5X and DDR5 that you had to think about when designing the core?

items.content:
Open models should outlive the places that host them. LibreAGI is a private BitTorrent tracker where members keep copies of the models most likely to disappear.

Credit grows with size and time, and a model with one copy earns four times the base rate. The rare ones need the most help.

Any format, from safetensors and GGUF to ONNX, under Apache-2.0, MIT or the Qwen Community License. Each file is checked against its source commit, and staff review every model.

A signed public catalog lists every model, hash and source, so anyone can rebuild the swarms if this site goes away.

The public channel is open to anyone, with no account needed. Come and ask questions before you apply.
